name: Lethal Congenital Contracture Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Lethal Congenital Contracture Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of multiple congenital joint contractures (arthrogryposis multiplex congenita)
Evidence of fetal akinesia or decreased fetal movements
Neonatal death typically within hours to days after birth
Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes such as GLE1
Severe respiratory insufficiency due to pulmonary hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple congenital joint contractures, fetal akinesia, and early neonatal lethality; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for GLE1 mutations is confirmatory; prenatal ultrasound may detect decreased fetal movements and joint contractures.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple congenital joint contractures (arthrogryposis multiplex congenita)
Fetal akinesia (reduced or absent fetal movements)
Severe respiratory insufficiency due to pulmonary hypoplasia
searchTerms: severe breathing failure from small lungs
respiratory insufficiency due to pulmonary hypoplasia
critical lung underdevelopment causing breathing issues

common.symptomName: Facial dysmorphism including micrognathia and low-set ears

searchTerms: too much amniotic fluid in pregnancy
excess fluid around fetus before birth
loss of muscle bulk and size
baby smaller than expected in womb

occasional.symptomName: Mild facial clefts or palate abnormalities
searchTerms: small facial clefts or palate problems
minor facial split or palate abnormality

laboratory: Normal routine laboratory tests; no specific biochemical markers
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing decreased fetal movements and joint contractures
Postnatal skeletal X-rays demonstrating joint contractures and bone abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in GLE1 gene (most common)
Other genes associated with fetal akinesia syndromes may be implicated
other: Electromyography may show decreased muscle activity
Muscle biopsy reveals hypoplasia and fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Sequence of anomalies due to decreased fetal movement
May have overlapping features but different genetic etiology
Often associated with other syndromic findings

redFlags: Absent or severely reduced fetal movements
references: Lahtinen AM et al. Mutations in GLE1 cause lethal congenital contracture syndrome. Nat Genet. 2008.
Hall JG. Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita: etiology, genetics, classification, diagnostic approach, and general aspects. J Pediatr Orthop B. 1997.
